title: A Ledger for the Confession Anew
premise: Oscar Vane, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives a confession letter for a murder committed forty years ago — postmarked the day after the victim's long-delayed funeral, and written in a hand that matches documents Oscar themselves catalogued. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Oscar discovers the killer has been quietly editing the cathedral's records for decades, erasing themselves from every ledger. The trap Oscar sets in the locked crypt forces a final choice between exposing the truth and protecting the person they've come to love; in the end, Oscar closes the case by letting the confession stand — but chooses not to name the lover who helped them find it.
about_author: Hazel Nystrom is a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing centuries of baptismal and burial registers before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who keep secrets professionally, and lives within earshot of a church bell she refuses to identify.

chapters.title: Postmarked After the Grave
chapters.summary: Oscar Vane's POV. A confession letter arrives naming a 1984 death ruled accidental, postmarked one day after the victim's reburial. Oscar, bound by professional pride to close what they open, begins cross-referencing the letter against the crypt ledgers and finds a page razored out. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession as duty overrides instinct to walk away.

chapters.title: The Hand That Filed Itself Away
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with interludes from Sister Maren, the cathedral's aging sacristan. The confession's handwriting matches catalogued documents — including ones Oscar processed years ago, meaning the killer works or worked inside. Maren shares fragments of the old scandal: an inheritance dispute over land beneath the crypt. Beat: intimacy grows between Oscar and Maren even as suspicion narrows toward her.

chapters.title: What the Statute Cannot Bury
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With days left before the statute expires, Oscar discovers the excised ledger page hidden in a reliquary lining: proof the victim was murdered for refusing to sign away the inheritance, and that the signatory was Maren's mother. Confronting Maren shatters their trust. Beat: love against duty at full collision — Oscar must decide whether the law or the truth matters more.

chapters.title: A Ledger for the Confession Anew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax in the sealed crypt. Oscar stages a false ledger entry claiming the original page survived, luring the true killer — the cathedral's lawyer, executor of the stolen inheritance — into destroying evidence before witnesses. The killer confesses; the statute expires mid-arrest, but the confession itself becomes the record. Beat: resolution through truth preserved, love spared, and a new ledger opened.
